relay: One of you holds the lantern high while the other feels along the drowned stair.
One of you braces the rusted grate while the other reaches through it for the latch.
One of you counts the choir's breathing while the other crosses on the silent beat.
One of you pays out the rope at the pit's lip while the other goes down into the dark.
You take the salt cask together, one prying the lid and one reading the mark beneath.
One of you cups the flame from the drip while the other works the seized bolt free.
One of you sings back to the sunk choir while the other passes beneath their chains.
One of you holds the chain taut over the black water while the other walks it across.
You share the lantern, one feeding the wick as it gutters and one tracing the bone map.
One of you leans on the bell rope while the other stills the clapper with a knife.
One of you stands in the cold spill of the cistern while the other bails from above.
One of you holds the drowned door from swinging shut while the other crawls through.
One of you rattles a far chain to draw the eyes while the other slips past the cage.
One of you kneels as a step at the wall of ribs while the other climbs to the ledge.
One of you turns the rusted wheel while the other catches the pin before it drops.
You raise the bucket in turns, one calling the count down the shaft and one on the rope.
One of you reads the map aloud while the other walks the dark by its words.
One of you steadies the ladder in the current while the other climbs to the hatch.
One of you feeds the rope through the ring while the other hauls the cage up.
One of you whistles at the rats to draw them while the other crosses their nest.
One of you holds the ferry against the pier while the other loads the lantern oil.
One of you presses the stone in the wall while the other runs through the opening door.
One of you watches the sleeping keeper's eyes while the other lifts the keys.
One of you swings the lantern as a signal while the other answers from the far ledge.
One of you wedges the flood door with a spar while the other swims the passage.
One of you calls out the depth while the other lowers the anchor on its chain.
One of you cuts the net while the other pulls a tangled friend clear of the water.
One of you balances the scale with stones while the other takes the relic from it.
One of you blocks the draught with a cloak while the other lights the damp wick.
One of you counts the waves at the sea door while the other runs on the seventh.
One of you pins the chain to the floor while the other files through the lock.
One of you holds the sleeping hound's gaze while the other slips through the gate.
One of you reads the tide table while the other rows at the moment it names.
One of you shines the lantern into the mirror while the other follows the beam.
One of you keeps the choir's tune while the other finds the missing verse.
One of you pumps the bellows while the other beats the key flat on the anvil.
One of you holds the torn map together while the other traces the route with a finger.
One of you lies flat on the ice while the other crawls out over you to the hole.
One of you lifts the drowned bell's clapper while the other slips the key from inside.
One of you taps the wall for the hollow while the other listens with an ear to the stone.
vault: A bronze door weeps brine and the reliquary behind it is yours if the lock does not bite.
You see the strongroom's silver through a hand of black water and a curtain of chains.
Behind the barnacled grate you see a drowned crown and the choir beneath it is waking.
A whalebone chest sits sealed with pitch and something inside it shifts when you knock.
The reliquary holds a saint's finger and the hinge is set to snap on your careless hand.
An iron coffer sits in the sluice and the water climbs a finger each breath you take.
The sunk lord's vault is rich past counting and its lock wants a colder hand than yours.
Salt has crusted the treasury door and the crust you must break is holding the roof up.
A cage of bone hangs over the well and what glitters inside it is worth your fall.
The chained casket hums as your lantern nears and the chain will not stay slack for long.
Behind the black door lie the pearls of the sunk and the door will remember your face.
The cistern floor is paved with gold plate and the water over it shows you no bottom.
A stone jaw guards the treasury and you must pass its teeth twice, in and out again.
The drowned altar keeps its silver under a lid of rust and the rust is thin as your skin.
Amber glows in the reliquary and the hands that reached before yours are still there.
The strongroom door is old bronze and the one who raised it last lies under your feet.
A chest of drowned silver sits in the eel pit and the eels watch you as you lean in.
The reliquary opens to your hand only if you press it flat on the needle lock.
Gold coins fill the sunk font and its water numbs your hand before you reach the bottom.
A fist sized pearl rests in a stone fish's jaw that snaps shut when you breathe on it.
The captain's strongbox lies in a cabin whose door slams at you with every swell.
A crown of salt crystal sits on a skull that crumbles if you lift the crown wrong.
Behind the treasury wall you see a chamber whose floor is a crust over the flood.
A blue steel sword is salted into its stone and the same salt holds the roof above you.
The drowned chapel's offering box is full and its lid is wired to the bell above you.
A golden bell hangs in the flooded tower and its rope rots through as you climb it.
The drowned merchant's purse is still on its belt and the dead hand closes on your wrist.
Jewels line the whale's skull and its jaw rests on a single wedge beside your knee.
An amber lamp burns in the sealed tomb and it burns the air you came in to breathe.
The chain of office lies in the cistern among a hundred rusted copies you must sift.
A casket of rings waits at the well's foot and the rope that lowers you is braided hair.
The sunk abbot's staff is set with garnets and the lock that holds it bites your fingers.
Coins are packed into the drowned statue and it leans toward you as each one comes out.
Letters of credit wait in a vault whose door seals at the sound of your breathing.
The black pearl sits on a plinth of ice that melts from the warmth of your hand.
Gold leaf covers the drowned throne and the throne sits on a trapdoor under your feet.
A tithe chest waits under the sagging arch and your first pull on it shakes the stones.
The relic box hums when you lie and grows heavier with each lie told near it.
A cache of lamp oil and gold lies behind a grate the current pins shut against your arms.
The seal of the sunk city lies in the moat mud beside all who reached for it before you.
toll: The passage is a throat of rusted hooks and you leave a strip of skin to pass it.
The gate opens to blood alone and you press a cut palm to the salt of its lock.
The way runs under the water and you give it a lungful of breath to reach the far side.
The chain is rusted to a rasp and it takes the skin of your hands as you climb it.
A hedge of bone teeth fills the arch and you crawl through leaving blood on every point.
The tunnel is cold enough to burn and its walls take skin from whatever you touch.
The choir of the sunk asks a song of you and every note is breath you will not get back.
The stair runs with brine and every step opens the cuts on your feet again.
You wade the cistern chin deep and the cold takes your breath before you find the ladder.
A curtain of rusted chain hangs across the way and it bites every arm you part it with.
The door drinks before it opens and you feed it a thumb pressed to the iron spike.
You hold your breath through the flooded arch and the far side is farther than it looks.
The only way on is a pipe full of water and you must swim it on one breath.
The gate's handle is wrapped in wire and you hold it until the gate gives.
The only air in the flooded tunnel is a pocket the size of a hat, and you share it once.
The door is hot from some fire behind it and you push it open with your palms.
The smoke from the drowned forge fills the stair and you climb it blind and coughing.
The ferryman takes a tooth for the crossing and pulls one from your jaw without asking.
The salt wind in the chimney strips your lips raw as you climb into it.
The eel gate opens only to your hand held in the water until it is bitten.
The frozen stair burns the soles of your feet with every step up it.
The lock drinks from the hand that turns its key and your fingers come away white.
Nettles grow thick over the salt tunnel and sting every inch of skin you show.
You crawl the drain on your elbows and leave the skin of them on the stone.
A hot spring blocks the passage and you wade it though it scalds.
The only handhold on the cliff is a blade set in the stone and you close your fist on it.
The door opens for a tear, and the burned hand you pressed to it gives you one.
You take the wasp nest's corridor at a walk and let the stings land.
The coral arch is sharp as glass and the only way through is on your belly.
The ledge is a lip of flint and it cuts through your boots as you inch along it.
The black water here is full of stinging jellies and you swim it anyway.
The drowned guard wants a blow on the chin before the gate, and you take it.
The chimney is too tight for your coat and your coat is all that keeps the cold off.
The lever has rusted into a thorn and your grip on it opens the skin.
You hang from the sill by your fingertips while the ledge below you breaks away.
The bridge is gone and you cross on the rusted cable, feet bare, skin torn.
The vent spits salt steam and you walk through it with your face in your sleeve.
The stone jaws close a little on anyone passing, and they close on your arm.
You pull the splinter of bone from the lock and it tears a nail away with it.
The passage floor is hot iron from the forge below and you run across it.
open: A dry ledge runs along the flooded hall and your lantern reaches the far door.
The water here is only ankle deep and the stones under your feet are flat and even.
An old rope bridge crosses the gap and every plank of it holds when you test it.
The passage is low but dry and the choir's song is far off behind you.
A stair of cut stone climbs out of the wet and the rail holds when you lean on it.
The gate stands open on its chain and nothing stirs in the dark as you pass.
You pass a row of empty shackles and the only sound is the drip from the arch above.
A drift of salt crunches under your feet and the tunnel beyond it is straight and dry.
Your lantern finds a door already ajar and a cold clean draft comes through the gap.
The channel has drained to mud and you cross it on the ribs of a sunk barge.
The chain across the arch is rusted through and it comes away in your hands.
A drowned bell lies on its side and you walk over it to the dry stair beyond.
A dry gallery runs above the flood and its boards creak under you but hold.
The tunnel slopes gently up and you smell rain from somewhere above.
A row of lamps still burns along the causeway and lights your way between them.
The tide pool steps are dry at this hour and each one is wide enough for you to sit on.
A handrail of polished bone runs under your hand down a gentle ramp to the next hall.
The keeper's hut stands empty with its door open and its stove still warm for you.
A broken statue lies across the stream and its back makes you a dry bridge.
The corridor is lined with sleeping bats and none of them stirs as you pass.
The cavern opens wide and a thin light falls on you through a crack high overhead.
The well has a spiral stair inside its wall and every step of it takes your weight.
A line of chalk marks on the wall shows you the way a friend went safely.
The drowned market square has drained and you walk between its empty stalls.
A cart track runs straight through the tunnel and the ruts guide your feet.
The flood gate stands raised and the channel below it barely wets your boots.
Moss covers the stair and it is soft and quiet under your boots.
A chapel of dry stone sits above the waterline and its benches offer you rest.
The pipe is wide enough to stand in and dry for as far as your lantern reaches.
The ferry waits for you at the landing with its pole laid across the seats.
A ledge of flat rock skirts the whirlpool and keeps you well clear of its pull.
The ossuary is quiet and its skulls face the wall as if to let you by.
The storm has passed through the shaft and left the rungs clean under your hands.
A wooden walkway has been laid over the mud and every board is firm under you.
The black lake is still as glass and shallow enough to show you the path of stones.
The fog in the hall lifts as you enter and shows a clear floor to the far arch.
A crooked tree grows out of the wall and its roots give you a ladder to the ledge.
The drowned library is dry on its upper floor and its aisle leads you straight through.
The salt caves glitter in your lantern and the floor between the pillars is level.
A signpost of bone points you up and the way it points is open.
